To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ac conductivity of α-zirconyl phosphate intercalates of methyl and ethyl substituted derivatives of pyrazoles and pyrazole is lower than that observed with the corresponding unsubstituted compounds, while that of the imidazoles is lower than that found in the corresponding unsubstitututed compounds.
the intercalation of α-ZrP with substituted imidazole and substituted pyrazole decreases its ac conductivity by about one order of magnitude.
the ac conductivity of intercalation compounds of zrP with imazoles and pyrazoles decreases with the increasing basicity of the guest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation, characterization and ac conductivity of intercalation compounds with substituted pyrazole and substituted imidazole.
the synthesis and characterisation of intercalated zirconium phosphoates and with the ac conductivity of some intercalated derivatives.

the synthesis and the characterization of intercalation compounds of zirconoium phosphates with pyrazole and its methyl and ethyl substituted derivatives, imidazole and its mono- or di-methyl substituted derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the same guest, the conductivity of intercalate is higher when the host is α-ZrP than when it is γ-ZrP.
the ac conductivity of intercalated α-ZrP is higher than that of the γ-ZrP intercalates, but it is not correlated with the interlayer distance, the guest basicity or the intercalation mechanism.
the conductivity of the intercalates is determined by the proton mobility and, consequently, by the basicity of the intercalated species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intercalation of zirconium phosphate with imidazole or pyrazole derivatives decreases the proton conductivity by at least two orders of magnitude with respect to the parent α-ZrP intercalated with imidazole, but increases it by at least one with respect to γ-ZrP interlayered with imidazole.
the ac conductivity is a function of the interlayer distance and the protonation degree of the guests.

the conductivity of the intercalates of α-ZrP is much lower than that of γ-ZrPh, which is probably due to a higher degree of protonation of the former, but the conductivity of the former is much more sensitive to the substituent on the heterocyclic ring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interlayer distance of the host is not the only parameter affecting the ac conductivity, but the chemical structure of the guest is also important.
